column1: # blobExec blob denylist — blobs excluded from the rewrite by content id.
# A denylisted blob is never handed to the tokenizer. It is dropped from every
# rewritten tree, exactly like an oversized blob (Walker.readBlob), so the file is
# ABSENT from the tokenized repository rather than present as raw source: it
# produces no blame and no dataset row. It is counted separately from
# blobsOversized and blobsTimedOut, logged once with its sha, path and reason, and
# it does NOT affect the exit status. That last point is the difference between
# this list and a timeout: an entry here is a diagnosed, deterministic, cited
# exclusion, while a timeout is a hang nobody has explained yet and must keep
# blocking publication.
# This is a DATA file, not a constant in the code, so a paper can cite the list
# itself. It is loaded from the classpath (BlobDenylist.ResourcePath) and shipped
# inside the assembly jar, so adding an entry means editing this file and running
# `sbt assembly`. Nothing at run time can extend or override it: an undocumented
# exclusion is the one thing that would make the dataset's omissions unauditable.
# FORMAT: three TAB-separated fields. Blank lines and lines starting with # are
# ignored. Leading and trailing whitespace on a field is stripped.
#     <git blob sha1, 40 lowercase hex>  <citation>  <one-line reason>
# The key is the GIT BLOB id, which is what the walker has in hand
# (Walker.BlobMissTask.origId) and what blobExec's own timeout line prints. It is
# not the memo's key: tokenizeByBlobId/tokenBySha.pl hashes the file contents
# alone, with no git object header.
# The key is deliberately NOT the path. One of the entries below is the same
# source file at two different paths, moved by an OpenJDK repository
# reorganisation, and a path-keyed list would have to be updated every time a
# project moves a file. Content is the stable identity. The paths are recorded
# here for a reader rather than matched on:
#   test/langtools/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/classfile/TestNewCastArray.java
#       2ee2673ad0a8ff2cef0254e7bfdc488cc1d61a65   14,503 B
#   langtools/test/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/classfile/TestNewCastArray.java
#       504aaf9109fc01d6d62d99ac529ded99a8dfa8ca   14,451 B
# All four are historical versions of ONE file in tencent__tencentkona-21
# (OpenJDK-derived, 50,663 .java files at HEAD, 147,265 blobs recorded). It is a
# compiler regression test, @bug 8005681 "Repeated annotations on new,array,cast",
# whose stated purpose is to stress exactly the grammar that breaks the parser. It
# is not production source and carries no contributor-behaviour signal.
# The root cause is written up, with measurements and the upstream citation, in
# cregit-token-pipeline/.superpowers/sdd/peppy-pondering-music/
# srcml-nontermination-analysis.md. In short: srcML 1.1.0 does not terminate on a
# local variable declaration whose declared type is a multi-dimensional array
# carrying a type annotation on its first dimension when the initializer is an
# array-creation expression that also carries one — minimal reproducer
# `String @A [] [] s = new String @A [2] [2];`. It is non-termination, not
# slowness: 0 bytes of output, one core at 101%, resident memory flat at
# 10,544 kB, at every budget from 5 s to 600 s. Upstream srcML/srcML#2361 is open
# with no patch, and v1.1.0 (2025-08-14) is the latest release, so there is
# nothing to upgrade to. A working patch was built and validated at 12,016/12,016
# byte-identical blobs, and was deliberately NOT adopted, on provenance grounds:
# see srcml-upstream-fix-adjudication.md.
# Re-verified against the pinned binary on 2026-09-19: each of the four blobs
# produced 0 bytes and was killed at a 15 s budget.
# sha
2ee2673ad0a8ff2cef0254e7bfdc488cc1d61a65
column3: srcML 1.1.0 does not terminate on this file's annotated multi-dimensional array declarations (0 bytes out, killed at every budget from 5s to 600s); OpenJDK langtools regression test @bug 8005681, written to stress this grammar
